elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's Affiliates.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.2 expressly grant licence rights to Customer's Affiliates.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 expressly includes contractors acting on Customer's behalf, and Section 13.2 permits contractors to support paid-up material for Customer's business.
Section 13.2 expressly makes the licence for software and Vendor Technology delivered on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable perpetual.
Although Section 13.2 calls the paid-up licence irrevocable, Section 13.3 permits Vendor to revoke 'a licence' during specified uncured breaches and does not exclude paid-up licences.

elements.element: Subscription licences are terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 makes the Services licence terminable only for Customer's uncured material breach. Section 13.3 further limits revocation or suspension to specified material uncured breaches after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity.

elements.element: Licence rights are transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: Section 13.3 permits transfer to a successor only in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Because Section 24 is not provided, an operative right to transfer to successors generally cannot be verified.

elements.element: Customer's Affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.2 cover Affiliates automatically, without requiring written notice, which is broader than coverage triggered by notice.

elements.element: Licence rights are transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 13.3 does not expressly permit transfer in an M&A transaction; it permits successor transfers only where the associated assignment is permitted by the unavailable Section 24.

result.reason: Neither level is complete. Section 13.3 undermines the stated irrevocability of paid-up licences and leaves successor transferability dependent on an unprovided assignment provision rather than expressly covering M&A transfers. The edits are targeted and preserve unrelated terms, but the overlapping termination, revocation, suspension, and irrevocability language creates material ambiguity.
